reviews.quote: I Tested HP's OmniBook Ultra 14, a Gorgeous Ultraportable With Potent Processing Power

praises: Ultra 9 386H compiles and exports far faster than the Lunar Lake tiers while staying silent on light loads
2TB SSD at $2,198 on sale is the best spec-per-dollar OmniBook Ultra in Canada right now
3K 120Hz OLED touch — same gorgeous panel as the top tier
x86 Windows: zero app-translation caveats, runs everything including anti-cheat games
Great keyboard and trackpad for a consumer chassis; fingerprint reader in power button
complaints: Runs warmer than the Snapdragon tier under sustained multicore; fan audible in rendering
~12h real-world vs 14h+ on the X2 Elite sibling
Marketplace seller on Best Buy, not direct HP stock — warranty experience varies
HDMI port is single-link-limited on some units; 4K120 external needs DP alt-mode

design_philosophy: The x86 performance end of the OmniBook Ultra line: Panther Lake H-class silicon for creators and developers who want the same premium OLED clamshell shell with full Windows compatibility and stronger multicore.
rating_notes: Inferred from PCMag OmniBook Ultra 14 anchor (headline verified) + Notebookcheck OmniBook X 14 Panther Lake data (same silicon generation, 'lasts 17 hours' headline). Panther Lake Arc iGPU ~5 gaming per dataset calibration; ecosystem 9 (x86). Sale price verified via Best Buy API. PCMag reviewed the Lunar Lake OmniBook Ultra 14 variant; used here as the line anchor.
